text:
maria: quick heads-up — I have a reliable repro for the regression where comm/compute overlap disappears when we enable CUDA graph capture on multi-GPU runs.

sam: ok — what config? TP/PP, model, batch shape, nccl/driver?

maria: small repro: 7B transformer, TP=2, PP=1, seq_len=1024, dynamic batching (heuristic picks batch sizes 1/2/4), prefix KV cache enabled (we prefetch cached KV on a separate stream), NCCL 2.14, driver 535.86, CUDA 12.1. Redwood runtime branch: perf/graph-capture-experiments.

olivia: can you paste the nvprof/nsys capture snippet? curious where the streams are landing.

maria: pasted a trimmed nsys slice below — you can see compute kernels on stream 0, NVTX region "KV_prefetch" on stream 2, and NCCL all-reduce on stream 3. When we do a graph capture that includes both compute + the prefetch stream, the NCCL ops are serialized and scheduled after compute instead of overlapping.

```
Time    Stream  Activity
------  ------  -----------------------
0.00ms  s0      cudaLaunchKernel conv_fwd  (compute)
0.12ms  s2      memcopy async kv_prefetch   (prefetch stream)
0.14ms  s3      ncclAllReduce start       (comm stream)
0.16ms  s0      cudaLaunchKernel attn_dot  (compute)

--> expected: s3 NCCL overlaps s0 compute and s2 memcopy
--> observed during captured replay: s3 NCCL runs after s0 sequence finishes
```

maria: profiling notes: when capture is OFF, overlap is normal and step throughput is ~10% higher. With capture ON (capturing all streams including the prefetch), throughput drops and latency variance spikes.

derek: fwiw CUDA graph capture has restrictions: captured kernels must be launched on the same set of streams during replay, and some runtime libraries (NCCL) may insert implicit stream syncs when launched from a captured graph. Also capture may unify stream ordering.

sam: could the KV prefetch on a separate stream be changing stream ordering inside the graph? If capture records them in a different interleaving, NCCL might be forced onto the graph's default stream.

olivia: tried an experiment: moved KV prefetch onto the compute stream (no separate stream) and captured — overlap returned and perf improved. So separate prefetch stream during capture looks suspicious.

maria: another experiment: exclude NCCL ops from capture by using a two-phase approach: capture compute and mem ops, but launch NCCL outside the graph between graph replays. That also restores overlap, but we lose the end-to-end benefit of capturing comm launch latency.

perf-bot: perf/regression-alert — branch perf/graph-capture-experiments shows -9% throughput on multi-gpu capture job vs baseline (non-captured). See run: http://perf.internal/runs/1778501 (trace attached).

derek: theory: when capture includes cross-device comm, CUDA may convert queued NCCL enqueues into graph nodes that are serialized relative to preceding graph nodes. Also, some NCCL calls are not graph-safe and will get serialized to host-side enqueues. We should check for NCCL's stream association during capture.

sam: do we capture graphs per micro-batch or as a monolithic graph across batched sequence? Our batching heuristic sometimes merges variable-length requests which changes the kernel sequence between captures. Dynamic shapes are another vector.

maria: we capture per-config (seq_len, batch_size) but heuristic churn means we occasionally fall back to a different capture resulting in mixed graph replays vs fresh captures. That instability may be exposing ordering issues.

olivia: actionable experiments I ran and results: 
- Move KV prefetch to compute stream: overlap restored, +8% throughput.
- Capture compute-only (explicitly exclude prefetch and NCCL): overlap restored, but single-step latency slightly higher (+2ms) because NCCL launch cost now uncaptured.
- Force NCCL to use the same stream as compute via ncclComm->setStream (hack): overlap sometimes ok but observed spurious hangs in a couple runs.

maria: notes on kernel selection interaction: our runtime switches to a fused attention kernel under capture (it matches seq_len exactly). The fused kernel uses different workqueues and launches more small kernels; during capture the launch pattern changes, and NCCL nodes shift position. So kernel selection + capture interplay matters.

derek: plan: (1) add an explicit "graph-safe stream policy" in runtime: only capture kernels on streams that we can guarantee mapping for (compute stream, memcopy stream if certain), (2) avoid capturing NCCL/all-reduce nodes — instead record them separately and replay just compute graph, (3) change batching heuristic to prefer stable capture shapes for hotspots.

sam: +1. Also add runtime asserts: when capture is enabled log the stream-set we capture and raise a debug warning if KV prefetch uses a non-captured stream. That will make repros easier.

maria: I'll prototype a flag to disable capturing prefetch streams and land a small patch that forces KV prefetch onto compute stream during capture. If that looks stable we'll add policy-based capture selection.

olivia: I'll run a jittered stress test (1000 steps) across TP=2/4 and PP=1/2 to check for rare serialization hangs after forcing compute-stream prefetch.

perf-bot: test-scheduler queued jobs: graph-capture-stability (maria), graph-capture-stress (olivia).

sam: FYI we should also validate with latest NCCL 2.15 — sometimes NCCL fixes graph interactions.

maria: thanks. Owner: maria will push a small runtime flag. Derek will prototype capture-policy, Olivia will run stress, Sam will validate with newer NCCL. Will report back with timelines tomorrow. :eyes: :bug:

(reacted :thumbsup: by sam, :eyes: by olivia)
